samples.task_summary: Predict whether an ACS person is employed using demographic, household, and disability-related attributes that should generalize across states.

scores.rationale: Age is a strong, stable predictor of labor force participation and employment across states.
Education is one of the most robust predictors of employment and is broadly portable across geographies.
Marital status has some stable association with employment, but it is indirect and weaker than core human-capital features.
Household relationship can proxy life stage and family role, but it is less directly tied to employment and can be noisy.
Disability status is a meaningful and fairly stable predictor of employment, though it is sensitive and may vary in measurement.
Employment status of parents is mainly relevant for children and is not a stable predictor for the target population.
Citizenship can correlate with employment, but it is also a demographic proxy and may reflect state-specific composition rather than causal stability.
Recent mobility may capture job-related moves, but it is noisy and can encode geography and local migration patterns.
Military service has some labor-market relevance but is sparse and not a broadly stable predictor.
Ancestry is a weak proxy that is more likely to encode demographic and regional artifacts than stable employment signal.
Nativity is somewhat predictive through labor-market integration, but it is a demographic shortcut with limited stable causal value.
Hearing difficulty can affect employability and is a reasonably stable health-related predictor.
Vision difficulty is similarly a stable functional limitation that can affect employment.
Cognitive difficulty is often strongly related to employment status and should generalize better than demographic proxies.
Sex has persistent association with employment but is a sensitive demographic attribute and can reflect structural bias.
Race may carry signal through structural labor-market differences, but it is a sensitive proxy and less desirable for stable generalization.
